title: National Ploughing Championship 2026
summary: Ireland's largest outdoor event returns to Screggan for the 95th edition from 15th-17th September 2026.
description: The National Ploughing Championship returns to Screggan, Tullamore, Co. Offaly from 15th to 17th September 2026 for the 95th edition. It is described as Ireland's largest outdoor event, taking place over three days. The event brings together farming, machinery, livestock, food, innovation, and entertainment. At the heart of the championship are national ploughing competitions where more than 350 competitors showcase their skills. Visitors can explore hundreds of trade stands featuring agricultural machinery, technology, home and garden products, food producers, crafts, education, and rural businesses. The event also includes livestock displays, forestry, sustainability, and innovation zones. Families can enjoy live entertainment, food demonstrations, shopping, children's attractions, and animal displays. There are opportunities to meet exhibitors from across Irish agriculture and rural life.

This month, the club presents a screening of 'The Lives of Others' on Wednesday 16 September at 6pm. The film was released in 2006 and is directed by Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck. Cartoonists to Caricature Galway Faces starts at 4.30pm at Town Hall Theatre, offering portraits and caricatures by Jim Cogan and Margaret Nolan. Other listed events include Blind Book Speed Friending at Plámás from 4pm and Eight Tonnes - Artists Reimagine Traditional Tractor Parades at St. Michael’s Square, Ballinasloe, starting at 9am.

title: Cahir Tradfest: Traditional Irish Music Weekend
summary: A weekend of traditional Irish music, song and dance with concerts, workshops, sessions and community events in Cahir.
description: Cahir Tradfest returns for a weekend of traditional Irish music, song and dance with concerts, workshops, sessions and community events taking place across the town. The festival begins on Friday evening with the official launch and a traditional music session in the Shamrock Lounge. On Saturday, musicians of all ages can take part in workshops at Bunscoil na Cathrach. The day continues with an evening concert at Cahir Castle featuring the Cahir Comhaltas Seisiún group, local musicians, singers and dancers. Whether you are a musician, regular session player or simply enjoy traditional Irish music, Cahir Tradfest offers plenty of opportunities to listen, learn and join in. The event is located at The Square, Cahir, Co. Tipperary, Ireland.

title: Ken O'Sullivan: Stories from the Sea
summary: A live show by filmmaker Ken O'Sullivan featuring his 25-year journey exploring the North Atlantic.
description: Ken O'Sullivan presents a live show titled Stories from the Sea, featuring his experiences exploring the North Atlantic Ocean and seas around Ireland. The event combines film and stories from his 20-plus year career, including personal insights from being surrounded by killer whales, swimming with dolphins, and encounters with fin and blue whales. O'Sullivan has produced more than twenty natural history documentaries for RTÉ, and his series North Atlantic was acquired by the BBC and broadcast in over 30 countries. He also features alongside David Attenborough in BBC Earth's Stunning Underwater Nature Footage, which has 7 million views on YouTube. The show pays homage to his family's 250-year history on Fenit Island, Co. Kerry, and discusses education and conservation, which have been central to his work since 2005. His documentaries are included in the secondary school exam curriculum for Junior Cycle Geography and Business Studies. His book, Stories from the Deep, is critically acclaimed for its writing and descriptions of nature. The event takes place at 15 MacCurtain Street, Victorian Quarter, Cork, from 19:30 to 21:10 on 26 September 2026.

title: Galway Cartoon Festival 10th Anniversary
summary: The 10th Galway Cartoon Festival takes place in October with workshops, exhibitions, and guests from Belgium.
description: The Galway Cartoon Festival is celebrating its 10th anniversary in October. The theme for this year is 'Having a Laugh'. A programme launch will be held on Tuesday 8th September from 5pm to 7pm at Kombu, Druid Lane, Galway City centre. The launch is open to the public for drinks, speeches, photos, and drawing. Glenn Marshall of Private Eye will attend and recreate the Wooden Horse of Troy. The festival features expert drawing workshops for both adults and children. Guests are coming from Belgium, where the European Cartoon Centre will present a history of Belgian art through cartoons. French satirist Nicolas Vadot, who contributed to the first festival poster, will speak about his career in television, animation, and editorial cartooning. The featured Irish artist this year is Fergus Boylan. A special celebratory exhibition at the Galway City Museum will review the highlights of the first ten years. The event also includes a new Bookshop Trail, an exhibition and panel discussion marking the passing of The Phoenix magazine, cartooning coffee mornings, Irish language workshops, a dedicated exhibition of cartoons in Gaeilge, games, films, and an annual trip to Inis Oírr.

title: Elf Town Dublin 2026 at the RDS
summary: Two magical Santa experiences returning to the RDS in November and December 2026.
description: Elf Town Dublin returns to the RDS for selected dates throughout November and December 2026. Families can choose between two experiences, both ending with a beautifully immersive, private, and personalised family visit with Santa. The new 'The Magical Santa Visit' is a shorter 30-minute option. It includes a visit to the Frozen Forest, The Ice Cave, and The Elf Town Toy Shop where every child picks a toy from over 100 options. Attendees receive a personal Elf Town Hat and Name Badge. Tickets for this experience start at €10 per adult and €18 per child. The longer 'Elf Town Immersive Experience' features meeting real reindeer, writing a letter to Santa in the Post Office, baking cookies with Mrs Claus, theatrical performances, and partying with elves at the Town Square, also ending with the Santa visit. Tickets for this journey start at €19 per adult and €29 per child. Flexible monthly payment plans are available. A competition to win a Family Pass opens on Tuesday 21 July 2026.
